summary: An Indologist, Thomas Lumisden Strange studied at Westminster School and the East India Company College between 1824 and 1826.
Working in Indology and linguistics, Thomas M. Hunter served as Dean at the University of Virginia and held an attested post at the University of British Columbia in 2011.

Thomas Malten is an Indologist and linguist who completed his doctoral studies under Ayyadurai Dhamotharan. In 1991, he held attested posts at both the University of Cologne and Heidelberg University.
Thomas Manning was a scholar in Tibetology and sinology. He studied at Westminster Hospital and was a scholar at Gonville and Caius College from circa 1790 to 1795.

Thomas Maurice worked in Indology and history/archaeology, earning a B.A. and M.A. from the University of Oxford after studying at St John's and University Colleges. He served as Assistant-Keeper of Manuscripts at the British Museum from 1798 to 1824.

A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, Thomas Nathan Patton earned a PhD from Cornell University, where he studied under Anne M. Blackburn. He held an attested post at the City University of Hong Kong in 2018.

An Indologist, linguist, and religious studies scholar, Thomas Oberlies studied under Paul Thieme and Albrecht Wezler. He taught at Zurich (1990), held posts at Tübingen and Freiburg, and became Arbeitsstellenleiter at Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Educated at Trinity College Dublin (B.A.) and the University of Edinburgh, Thomas Oldham worked in history and archaeology. He directed the Geological Survey of Ireland, was Professor at Trinity College Hartford, and served as Superintendent of the Geological Survey of India (1851-1876).

Thomas Procter was an Indologist who earned his B.A. from Jesus College, Oxford (1818-1824). He later served as a Fellow at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1824-1826) and Examiner at Fort William College in 1828.

Thomas R. Trautmann, a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology, studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He spent his career at the University of Michigan, serving as co-director (attested 1980) and later Professor Emeritus of History and Anthropology (attested 2012).
Thomas Robert Malthus was an academic who studied at Warrington Academy (~1782-1784), Jesus College, Cambridge (1784), and the University of Cambridge (~1784-1788).

Thomas Robinson studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (1808-1816), receiving his B.A., M.A., and D.D. Working in linguistics and other fields, he served as Lord Almoner’s Professor of Arabic at the University of Cambridge from 1837 to 1854.
Thomas Roebuck studied at the Royal High School and worked in linguistics and Indology. He served at the College of Fort St. George and was an Examiner at Fort William College (~1809-1819).

Linguist Thomas Sebeok studied at Chicago under Leonard Bloomfield and at Princeton under Roman Jakobson, earning a Ph.D. From 1943 to 1991, he served at Indiana University Bloomington, becoming Distinguished Professor Emeritus.
Thomas Seymour Burt was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Addiscombe Military Seminary (1821-1823) and served as a Major in the Bengal Engineers from 1824 to 1847.

Arnold studied at Magdalene College under Edward Byles Cowell. Working in history, religious studies, and other fields, he held posts at Aligarh Muslim University, Government College Lahore, University of the Punjab, the India Office, and SOAS University of London.

Thomas Watters was a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies who earned his B.A. at Queen's University Belfast/Queen's University of Ireland (1857-1861). He served in the HM Diplomatic Service from 1863 to 1895.

Clark studied at Nottingham, Cambridge, and SOAS under Rylands, Turner, and Page. He held successive posts at SOAS as Lecturer and Reader in Bengali between 1948 and 1962, and visited the University of Pennsylvania in 1961.

Educated at Wellington College and Sandhurst, Haig worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served in the Indian Civil Service, as Professor at Trinity College Hartford (~1923-1925), and as Persian Lecturer at SOAS.
Thomas Zehnder is an Indologist and linguist who completed his PhD at the University of Zurich under the supervision of Alexander Lubotsky.
